reader.requirement: On a sequential-organization READ, writing NEXT (with or without RECORD, INTO, AT END, NOT AT END, END-READ) must behave exactly as the same READ without NEXT; the later PREVIOUS alternative of the direction is not part of the 1985 format and must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the PREVIOUS alternative below COBOL-2002 (construct read-previous-2002, COBOL0900); the NEXT alternative is never gated

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: PREVIOUS is accepted at 2002 and later and refused at 1985; NEXT has no effect on a sequential file at every edition (BindRead sets ReadKind.Next for NEXT and for no direction alike)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f21_01 alternates NEXT and plain READs on a fixed-length file; NEXT with INTO on a variable-length file, NEXT at end and after at end, NEXT on an absent optional file, and the PREVIOUS refusal are not exercised

probes.printed: N1 [AB      ] 2 00 / N2 [CDEFGH  ] 6 00 / N3 AT END 10 / N4 46 / OPT OPEN 05 / OPT AT END 10
probes.expected: READ NEXT INTO / NEXT RECORD INTO deliver records 1 and 2 with their lengths; READ NEXT then gives at end 10 and, after it, 46 with neither phrase run; on an absent OPTIONAL file the first READ NEXT is at end 10, as a plain READ would

probes.printed: rdprev.cob(36,20): error COBOL0900: READ PREVIOUS requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: PREVIOUS is not in the 1985 READ format (§1985:VII.4.4.2 shows only [NEXT]) and is refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR2  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: SequentialIoBinder.BindRead maps both an explicit NEXT and an absent direction to ReadKind.Next, so the emitted READ is the same; only PREVIOUS changes the kind, and VersionConformancePass.VisitReadDirection refuses it at 1985. The probe outputs match plain-READ behaviour in every leg.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the 1985-only arm the reader did not combine with NEXT: OPEN INPUT ... REVERSED (1985 only). nx2.cob at --std 85 (runs/nx2-002): READ NEXT, READ NEXT RECORD, plain READ on a REVERSED file read backward exactly as a plain READ: 'R1 CCC 00 / R2 BBB 00 / R3 AAA 00', then READ NEXT INTO ... AT END ... NOT AT END ... END-READ at end 'R4 AE / R4 10' (INTO not executed); I-O mode READ NEXT / REWRITE / READ NEXT / REWRITE then a fresh OPEN INPUT and three READ NEXT: 'I2 BBB 00 / I3 00 / F ZZZ' (NEXT does not disturb the REWRITE-after-READ pairing). Later-edition forms refused: nx3.cob READ NEXT RECORD WITH NO LOCK -> 'error COBOL0900: a record-lock phrase ... requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)'; reader's rdprev.cob showed PREVIOUS -> COBOL0900. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR2  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2'.
